subject: english-literature
source_note: Topic structure follows the Cambridge IGCSE IGCSE Literature in English specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.blurb: A set prose text in passage and essay form

units.name: Drama
units.blurb: A set drama text in passage and essay form

units.name: Unseen / Coursework
units.blurb: Unseen criticism or a coursework portfolio

topics.name: Language, Imagery & Tone
topics.blurb: Analysing detail, imagery and poetic effect

topics.name: Study of a Set Prose Text
topics.blurb: Plot, character and theme of the prose text

topics.name: Prose Essay Response
topics.blurb: Whole-text essay on character, theme and method

topics.name: Study of a Set Drama Text
topics.blurb: Plot, character and theme of the play

topics.name: Drama Passage Response
topics.blurb: Extract-based close analysis of dramatic effect

topics.name: Drama Essay Response
topics.blurb: Whole-text essay on character, theme and dramatic method

topics.name: Unseen Poetry/Prose Criticism

connections.why: Close study of set poems develops the language-analysis skills examined
Analysing individual poems is the basis for comparing them
Imagery and tone analysis transfers directly to prose extracts
Knowing the whole text supports detailed passage analysis
Whole-text understanding underpins the essay response
Close-reading skills feed wider essay argument
Knowing the whole play supports analysis of key extracts
Whole-text understanding underpins the drama essay
Close analysis of scenes strengthens essay argument
Essay-writing technique on character and theme is shared across genres
Passage-based analysis uses the same close-reading discipline
Skills built on set poems are applied to unseen criticism
Extract analysis is exactly what the unseen paper assesses
Essay skills on set texts are extended in the coursework portfolio
Coursework draws on the same analytical essay technique
